title: CLO 2024 Course: Create Subculture Fisherman Hats and Unlock Your New Summer Trend!
description:
Unlock Your Trendy New Look with New Techniques  
CLO technical experts guide you through the detailed process of making various accessories, teaching you step-by-step how to create hats in subcultural styles with full skills!  
Join CLO and become a master of virtual fashion design!
transcript:
Let's officially start today's live broadcast.  
Hello, I am Joy, your host from Shanghai.  
Today, I will be demonstrating the making of this subculture servant hat.  

First, let's take a look at the hat model we want to create.  
It is a basic bucket hat shape, with some decorations added to complete the design.  

Let's first open the live broadcast materials.  
You can access the materials by scanning the QR code at the bottom left corner of the screen and following our official account.  
Then reply to get the live broadcast materials for this session.  

Okay, now we officially start the live broadcast.  
First, we will import a model from this material package.  
We are going to make this hat.  
Since the copy file is not included here, we have to create it ourselves.  

We first need to measure the model’s head.  
Using the virtual model tool, we set a point in front of the model, then press Shift to set a second point, which will create a circle.  
We tilt the circle slightly because our hat won't be completely flat.  
Currently, the measurement shows 530 points, approximately 54 centimeters around the head.  

We will create a 54 cm head base plate.  
Using the virtual tool, click on an empty area and input the width value.  
Since the head circumference is 54 cm, the width is half of that, 27 cm (270 mm), dividing the hat front and back.  
The height is set to 90 cm.  

We extend this plate by selecting the sides that need extension and choose all directions.  
Modify the upper side length to 250 mm (25 cm), while the bottom corresponds to the head circumference of 54 cm.  
Click OK, and the plate is created.  

Next, create another plate using the virtual tool, with width 270 mm and height 60 mm (should be 96 cm as per original, but possibly a typo; assuming 60 mm height here).  
Move this plate slightly, extend all directions, and modify line 2 length to 380 mm.  
Click OK.  

After creating these two plates, we make a top plate.  
Select the circle tool, enter a diameter of 500 mm (50 cm), which matches the head measurement.  
Confirm and align the plates using Ctrl + D shortcut to mirror the other side.  

Now, create the small "bull's feet" plate using the hexagonal tool.  
Set a point in the blank area, hold Shift to keep it vertical, draw the shape, use the right mouse button to exit drawing mode, and set the length to 48 mm.  
Draw the shape resembling the small bull's foot and adjust the hexagonal tool slightly to smooth its curves.  

Place the bull's foot plate, set the outer circumference line, then create an internal line with a diameter of 2 mm for convenience.  
This internal line will be useful because on the hat you can see a name line, which we will also create.  

Make another plate copy by duplicating with Ctrl + D, unlock its connection, and arrange all plates on the model's head accordingly.  
Select a plate, press Ctrl + A to activate positioning, drag the positioning ball upwards without disturbing the layout.  
Press Shift + F to open arrangement points.  
Arrange the front plate first, set its shape type to flat, then rotate it using world coordinates for convenience.  

Switch to the back view by pressing key 8 and arrange the back plate similarly by flipping it over.  
After arranging front and back plates, arrange the cap plate on top, also set to flat.  

For the two small bull's feet plates, don't sew them on yet; skip arranging them for now.  
Move to the sewing step.  

Use a combination of 3D and 2D windows for sewing.  
Select the edge completely, then select the cap with Shift to select multiple edges.  
Do the same for the back edges, then sew the small bull's feet plates to the hat.  
Set the internal line diameter to 2 mm.  

This internal line helps with sewing.  
If you don’t remove one of the joints between the two bull’s feet plates beforehand, the sewing line may incorrectly sew symmetrically between them.  
So, remove one joint in advance.  

After sewing, remember to set the sewing line to fold.  
Select the two small bull's feet plates, right-click the small square in the middle of the positioning ball and add them to the side so they follow the sewing line position.  

Next, add fabric to the plates.  
Open the fabric maker from the main menu bar.  
Enter the fabric name as "Danning" and the supplier as you prefer.  
Select the fabric type "Danning cloth," with ingredients: 70% cotton, 19% other fibers.  
The fabric maker will auto-fill the rest, enter fabric weight as 230 grams.  

This sets the fabric’s physical attributes for simulation.  

For fabric stickers, if you have physical fabric samples, scan them and apply related PVR stickers.  
Alternatively, use cloud-predicted fabrics from the pre-purchased materials list.  

Apply physical attributes to the fabric and confirm.  
From the fabric library, select your preferred fabric and apply it to the current fabric.  

Add a print sticker if needed by clicking and placing it, adjusting opacity as necessary.  

For the small bull’s feet, use leather fabric.  
Search for leather in the fabric window, find Puku sheepskin, drag it onto the plate, and apply.  
Adjust fabric properties: lower shadow intensity, increase shadow brightness to make it close to white, so the background color isn’t affected.  

Choose a red color from the default palette for color adjustment, then copy this fabric and change its color to black for another plate.  
Apply the black fabric to the corresponding plate.  

Select the two cowhide plates and press Ctrl + Shift + B to create the back side of the plate inside.  
Flip it over to add to the surface.  

Improve the clothing quality for the whole hat and simulate.  
Adjust fill-in thickness for the cowhide plates to 5 to create a bulging effect between the two plates.  
Simulate again.  

Switch the clothing simulation type to translucent surface for the whole hat.  
Rotate the hat slightly using policy view on the digital keyboard for a better angle.  

From the top view, observe the effect, which looks straighter.  
Overlay the translucent surface on the thick texture surface and continue working.  

The hat should have a small step-like outline.  
Use the edge sewing line for the round part and set folding angles: 240 degrees (greater than 180°, curves inward) for the main line, and 150 degrees for the inner line.  
Simulate to see a small curve line on the hat’s side for realism.  

Adjust angles as needed, but generally keep the middle line folding angle above 180°, and the inner side lines below 180°.  

Use the sewing machine tool to find the 3D sewing line with a curve on one side, ensuring it’s line A as needed.  
To better view, switch to black-and-white surface mode.  

Although there is a guiding seam here, the effect is not very clear visually.  
Adjust rendering thickness based on fabric thickness (about 0.5), set rendering thickness to 0.8 for a thicker look.  
Switch to dense texture surface to see the pressed seam effect.  

After finishing the indentation and guiding seam, add the overall fashion line on the hat brim.  
Select the brim edge, set internal line spacing to 10 mm, and expansion count to 5, dividing the 60 mm width evenly.  

After setting, cut the two plates with linked operation and clone the inside layer using Ctrl + Shift + B.  
Delete side overlapping seams because the cloned inner layer will automatically sew overlapping seams, but remove these side overlaps to separate inside and outside seams.  

Simulate to check the effect: a slight indentation appears, but more puffing might be needed depending on actual craftsmanship.  
Use conflict thickness to add a slightly protruding effect.  

Set conflict thickness to 3 and simulate again to see a more pronounced effect.  

Add a welding belt inside the hat using the lifting tool (shortcut S).  
Set width to 1 cm (head circumference 54 cm minus 1 cm = 530 mm), height to 3 cm (30 mm).  

After creating the welding belt plate, select it and both top and bottom edges, right-click and find the internal section between lines, set expansion number to 2 to produce two lines.  

Apply cotton fabric from the Puku window to the welding belt, then change the color (it will update after pasting).  

Sew the welding belt using the sewing tool by selecting the edges and pressing Shift to select multiple edges, then fold and sew accordingly.  

Hide the model with Shift + A for better view.  
Adjust particle diameter to 5 and thickness to 1 for this plate, simulate again.  

The plate is simulated correctly but may face inward; flip it inside front for convenience when adding the name line later.  

Our Han Dai (hat) should be double-layered.  
Previously, this was done by layering clones; now we increase rendering thickness to simulate double layers.  
Set rendering thickness on relevant plates to 0.5 matching material thickness, then add the double-layer effect.  

Add the name line by using the name line tool and enable 3D view to see the curve, closer to real double-layer craft effect.  
Adjust diameter and set the line type to single-layer flat.  

Modify the material color to match the fabric color applied earlier.  

Follow this method to add name lines on other parts as well, including the hat body and brim where seams are pressed.  
Adjust diameter and internal line distance to control name line placement, usually set expansion to 1 and diameter to 5.  

Add sewing marks using a black background image imported as texture, then automatically generate hair lines.  
Remove the black background and replace it with a transparent one for actual sewing mark.  

Adjust snowflake effect on the hat surface, turning it lighter and less red.  
Add snowflake effects on other parts as needed.  

Apply decorations, starting with a missing bull’s horn thread.  
Set it to appear only on one surface or both sides as needed.  

Apply snowflake decorations on both sides of the hat accordingly.  

Modify surface roughness to lower, increase reflection intensity to enhance plastic feel on certain lines.  
Change line color to black to match buttons.  

Add cross-stitching by creating rectangles based on internal lines, rotate by 90 degrees using the edit tool, delete unnecessary lines, merge points to close boxes, and adjust position slightly.  

Right-click lines to add cross-stitch boards and sewing lines, arrange vertically with Shift.  

Make an edge and pudding effect by copying the Danning fabric and applying it only to the edge board, adjusting particle diameter to 5 and thickness to 1 or 0.8, similar to the main hat fabric.  

Change the edge fabric’s plant light type to hair, then dye it white by adjusting shadow intensity and brightness in the dye window.  
Set luminosity adjustments and smoothness accordingly, enabling gravity and setting brightness to 0.5.  

Add a chain decoration by first creating a version of the chain plate.  
Cut the inner line at 20 mm width and 2 mm, delete unnecessary parts and inner lines.  

Zoom in, apply new values, and add the chain plate to the workspace.  
Use the current thread to remove and add the chain to the board, sew it to the front side of the hat.  

Select sewing lines and set to fold, right-click the board and add it to the outside.  

Adjust opacity to 0 to hide underlying fabric, visually leaving only the chain visible.  

Adjust chain position closer to the front side of the hat for a drawn-on appearance.  

Add metal buttons at the chain start points, change their type to metal, adjust size and position, set width to 13 mm, and apply to both sides.  

Make holes for window rings using the inner circle; create holes with diameter 16 mm.  
Move cut lines to position, applying transparent fabric on cut plates.  

Add smoke effect on transparent plates, set size to 10, keep thickness consistent with fabric.  

Change material to metal, switch to screen coordinate system for easier positioning from perspective.  

Duplicate and position metal rings symmetrically on both sides.  

Use glue (adhesive setting) for metal rings to ensure firm attachment to the dial, preventing displacement.  

Adjust ring positions as needed.  

After cutting plates, the sewing wrinkles disappear; wrinkles can be added later if desired.  

Perform the same wrinkle setting on the other side.  

Remove the head mask by pressing Shift + A and compare with the reference picture.  

Add a fixed line in the middle using the free thread tool if needed, adjust spacing to 0.8 for better appearance.  

Finally, review the overall rendering effect.  
The 3D window may display effects more obviously than the rendering window, so pay attention to such differences.  

That concludes the production of this hat.  
Thank you for joining today’s live broadcast.  
I hope you have learned something about making this hat.  

Okay, that’s all. Goodbye, everyone!

chunks.content: ## Overview of Subculture Fisherman Hat Creation This section introduces the process of creating a subculture fisherman hat, outlining the basic bucket hat shape with decorative enhancements. It covers the initial setup, including model import and head measurements, essential for accurate hat design in CLO 2024. --- ## Model Import and Head Measurement The hat design begins by importing a base model from the material package. Since no pre-made copy file exists, it must be created manually. Using the virtual model tool, measure the model’s head circumference by setting two points in front of the model, creating a slightly tilted circular measurement. - Head circumference measured: 530 points (~54 cm). - Create a head base plate modeled as half the head width (27 cm or 270 mm) by 90 cm height. - Extend the plate in all directions, setting the upper side length to 250 mm (25 cm), with the bottom matching the 54 cm circumference. These measurements ensure the hat fits the virtual model accurately. --- ## Plate Creation and Arrangement Three main plates are created to form the hat structure: 1. **Head Base Plate:** Width 270 mm, height 90 cm, extended to match head shape. 2. **Second Plate:** Width 270 mm, height 60 mm; extended and adjusted to 380 mm on one side. 3. **Top Plate:** Circular plate with a diameter of 500 mm (50 cm), matching head circumference. A "bull’s feet" decorative plate is created using the hexagonal tool: - Drawn with Shift to maintain verticality. - Length set to 48 mm. - Outer circumference and internal 2 mm diameter lines are created to correspond with the hat's name line. Mirroring (Ctrl + D) is used to duplicate plates symmetrically. Arranging plates on the model’s head involves: - Activating positioning mode (Ctrl + A). - Dragging positioning balls for adjustment. - Rotating plates with world coordinates. - Front and back plates are arranged by flipping and setting shape type to flat. - Small decorative plates are not sewn initially to avoid misalignment. --- ## Sewing Technique and Internal Line Setup Sewing combines 3D and 2D window views for accuracy: - Select edges for front, back, and top plates. - Sew small bull’s feet plates separately. - Internal lines of 2 mm diameter act as guides to prevent sewing errors. - Remove one joint between bull’s feet plates before sewing to avoid symmetrical sewing lines. - Sewing lines are set to fold to simulate realistic fabric folds. - Positioning balls are used to align plates following sewing lines. --- ## Fabric Application and Properties Setup Fabric characteristics are set using the fabric maker tool: - Fabric name: "Danning" - Supplier: User-preferred - Type: Danning cloth - Composition: 70% cotton, 19% other fibers - Weight: 230 grams Fabric physical attributes influence simulation behavior. For fabric stickers: - Physical fabric samples can be scanned and applied via PVR stickers. - Alternatively, cloud-predicted fabrics from a pre-purchased list are available.

internal line spacing set to 10 mm. - Expansion count set to 5, dividing 60 mm width evenly. - Plates cut and inside layers cloned (Ctrl + Shift + B). - Side overlapping seams removed to separate inside and outside layers. - Conflict thickness set to 3 to enhance puffing effect. - Simulation repeated for visual confirmation. --- ## Welding Belt Creation and Sewing A welding belt is added inside the hat: - Created with lifting tool (shortcut S). - Width: 1 cm less than head circumference (530 mm). - Height: 3 cm (30 mm). - Internal sections created with expansion number 2 to form two lines. - Fabric applied from Puku cotton fabric library; color adjusted post-application. - Sewn by selecting edges and folding sewing lines. - Particle diameter set to 5 and thickness to 1 for simulation. - Plate flipped inside front for easier name line addition. --- ## Double-Layer Effect and Name Line Addition Double-layer effect is simulated by: - Increasing rendering thickness to 0.5, matching fabric thickness on relevant plates. - Name lines added using the name line tool in 3D view. - Diameter and line type set to single-layer flat. - Material color adjusted to match fabric. - Name lines applied on hat body and brim near pressed seams. - Typical settings: expansion 1, diameter 5, internal line distance adjusted. --- ## Sewing Marks and Surface Decoration Sewing marks created by: - Importing a black background image as texture. - Automatically generating hair lines. - Removing black background to make marks transparent.

chunks.content: - Name lines added using the name line tool in 3D view. - Diameter and line type set to single-layer flat. - Material color adjusted to match fabric. - Name lines applied on hat body and brim near pressed seams. - Typical settings: expansion 1, diameter 5, internal line distance adjusted. --- ## Sewing Marks and Surface Decoration Sewing marks created by: - Importing a black background image as texture. - Automatically generating hair lines. - Removing black background to make marks transparent. Snowflake effects added to hat surfaces: - Adjusted for lighter tone and reduced redness. - Applied selectively to various parts. Decorations include: - Missing bull’s horn thread added; visibility set to one or both sides. - Snowflake decorations applied symmetrically. - Surface roughness lowered and reflection intensity increased for plastic-like line effects. - Line color changed to black for button matching. --- ## Cross-Stitching and Edge Effects Cross-stitching created by: - Drawing rectangles based on internal lines. - Rotated 90° using the edit tool. - Unnecessary lines deleted; points merged. - Boxes arranged vertically with Shift for alignment. - Cross-stitch boards and sewing lines added via right-click menu. Edge and pudding effects: - Danning fabric copied and applied only to edge boards. - Particle diameter set to 5, thickness to 1 or 0.8. - Edge fabric light type set to hair. - Dyed white by adjusting shadow intensity and brightness. - Luminosity and smoothness configured; gravity enabled with brightness at 0.5. --- ## Chain Decoration and Metal Button Attachment Chain decoration procedure: - Chain plate created by cutting inner lines (20 mm width, 2 mm). - Unnecessary parts and inner lines deleted. - Chain plate added to workspace; thread adjustments made. - Sewn to front side of the hat with sewing lines set to fold. - Chain plate added to the outside surface. - Opacity adjusted to 0 to display only the chain visually. - Chain positioned closer to the front for drawn-on effect. Metal buttons: - Added at chain start points. - Metal type selected; size and position adjusted. - Width set to 13 mm. - Applied symmetrically to both sides. --- ## Window Rings and Smoke Effects Window rings: - Created using inner circle tool for holes with diameter 16 mm. - Cut lines moved to position holes correctly. - Transparent fabric applied to cut plates. - Smoke effect added on transparent plates with size 10; thickness consistent with fabric. - Material changed to metal. - Screen coordinate system used for easier perspective positioning. - Metal rings duplicated and symmetrically positioned. - Adhesive (glue) setting applied to metal rings for firm attachment, preventing displacement. - Ring positions adjusted as needed. --- ## Wrinkle Settings and Final Adjustments - After cutting plates, sewing wrinkles disappear but can be added later if desired. - Wrinkle settings duplicated on the opposite side. - Head mask removed (Shift + A) to compare with reference images. - Fixed line added in the middle with free thread tool.
